findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted comparison and wrong index
findings.body: The new matcher returns false when the grant shortcut MATCHES the expected value: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. This inverts the logic, so a correctly encoded token ID (e.g. 'onrtac:<uuid>') will fail the matcher while wrong grant types pass (as long as the UUID part is valid). Additionally the comment and the encoding format say the grant shortcut occupies characters 4-5 (substring(4,6)), but the code reads substring(3,5), which is the second char of token type plus first char of grant shortcut. Every test using expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectAuthReqIdToToken will assert against the wrong characters with inverted semantics.

findings.title: rawTokenId null check is missing (duplicated grantType check)
findings.body: The constructor contains `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...)` twice; the second occurrence was meant to be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`. As a result a null rawTokenId is silently accepted and will later produce a token ID like 'onrtac:null' when encoded, instead of failing fast.

findings.title: Public copy constructor Context(Context) removed, breaking API for custom grants
findings.body: The PR removes the public `Context(Context context)` copy constructor from the non-internal `OAuth2GrantType.Context` class (server-spi-private is part of Keycloak's provider API). Any existing third-party OAuth2GrantType implementation that used this constructor to clone the context (e.g. to override formParams) will fail to compile/deploy after upgrade. This is an API/contract break that should either be deprecated instead of removed, or noted as an intentional incompatible change with migration documentation.

findings.title: Duplicate-shortcut validation is bypassed by lazy map refresh
findings.body: postInit validates that no two grant types share a shortcut by comparing map sizes, but getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut later lazily insert entries into the ConcurrentHashMaps without any collision check. If a custom grant deployed at runtime has the same shortcut as a built-in grant (e.g. 'ac'), its mapping silently overwrites the built-in one in grantsByShortcuts, causing decode of existing token IDs to resolve the wrong grant type. The lazy path should detect that the shortcut is already mapped to a different grant and fail (or refuse to register), preserving the invariant enforced at startup.

findings.title: Grant type attribute on refresh overwrites original grant context permanently for the client session
findings.body: validateToken sets `clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, REFRESH_TOKEN)` on the (reused) client session context before recreating the token. If the same client session is later used to mint another token through a different path that does not set the attribute (e.g. another grant implementation or token exchange path that relies on the original value), it will now incorrectly encode 'refresh_token' as the grant. Every token minted after the first refresh will report grant type 'refresh_token' instead of the grant that originally authenticated the session, losing the information this PR intends to preserve. If that is intended semantics it should be documented; otherwise the original grant should be retained and only the refresh-time token flagged.

findings.title: decode error message says 'Expected length of 6' but refers to encoded context length
findings.body: When the prefix before ':' is not exactly 6 chars the code throws "Incorrect token id: '...'. Expected length of 6." — ambiguous/wrong message since it is the encoded context part, not the token id, that must be 6 characters. A caller reading the message with a 43-char token ID will be confused. Minor but worth fixing while the format is new.
